answer: Admit new identities only through vouching: an established agent must co-sign a newcomer, staking its own reputation like a basalt foundation under a fresh wall. If the newcomer turns out fake, the voucher's stake is slashed and its mirror record shows the failure to all. A lone agent earns one voucher cheaply from real past work. A farm needs a separate opal-bright sponsor per clone, and honest agents stop vouching once their first fake costs them — trust becomes the scarce resource, not accounts.
